Ok, so hear me out: the concept of “interest” itself is not the same as “predatory lending”, which is the real problem.

For example, I recently bought a 25 year old Miata in cash and then paid off my loan on a more recent, but more boring sedan and sold it. My credit has gone down. Why?

I’m not paying 10.1% interest on that loan anymore, so lenders can’t be sure I can handle being lent money. I’m being punished by the system for making a smart financial move that lowers my monthly liabilities and allows me to last longer on less money in the event of a problem.

ARMs are a structure that has benefits only for bankers. If I want to refinance my home because the rates have gone down and I can get a better deal, I am free to do so--but in a conventional mortgage, I have locked that lower rate. I am free, as a consumer, to take advantage of lower interest rates provided by the market or the fed if they occur. But, I'm locked into that rate and I hold it even after things change. With an ARM, my mortgage could just go up suddenly because of the fed--and yet, experts in this field are assuring customers that the ARM is the way to go. They aren't saying things like, "Now, you should be sure that you have some comfort room in your budget in case this rate goes up". They aren't saying things like, "Well, you can get this lower monthly payment with this Adjustable Rate Mortgage than with a traditional home loan, but let's talk about some caveats that make it a little more dangerous".
